title: What the compiler checks in a condition

questions.stem: Why does this page say the "Yoda condition" `0 == x` matters less in Java than in C?

options.text: Java compares literals by identity, so `0 == x` can be slower than `x == 0`
options.says: The page says the two forms are logically equivalent and give the same result.

options.text: Java rejects most accidental assignments there, as a condition must be boolean
options.says: The page says the compiler catches most of these errors, because a condition must be a boolean.

options.text: Java reorders both operands at compile time, so either order reads the same
options.says: The page gives readability, not any reordering, as the reason to prefer `x == 0`.
